title: Prescriptions Store Rule Sheet: Will-Call Hold, Photo ID and Who May Collect
content:
At a Kestrel store, a filled prescription under Kestrel Prescriptions waits in will-call for a number of calendar days set by its handling class, and the class also decides whether photo ID is needed, whether a caregiver may collect, and how old the person collecting must be.

| Handling class | Will-call hold (calendar days from the ready date) | Patient shows government photo ID | Caregiver may collect | Caregiver shows government photo ID | Minimum age of the person collecting (whole years) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Controlled Acute Prescription | 10 | No | Yes | No | 16 |
| Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription | 10 | No | Yes | No | 16 |
| Schedule V Controlled Prescription | 10 | Yes | Yes | Yes | 18 |
| Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription | 10 | Yes | Yes | Yes | 18 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 7 | Yes | Yes | Yes | 18 |
| Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription | 5 | No | Yes | Yes | 18 |

- **Will-call hold** — the calendar days a ready fill waits in will-call, counted from its ready date, before it is returned to stock.
- **Patient photo ID** — whether the patient must show government photo ID to collect a fill.
- **Caregiver** — whether someone other than the patient may collect a fill, and whether that caregiver must show government photo ID.
- **Minimum age** — the minimum age in whole years of the person collecting a fill.

## Counter cases (hypothetical)

- A 17-year-old collecting a Non-Controlled Acute Prescription meets the class minimum of 16; the same person collecting a Schedule V Controlled Prescription does not meet that class's minimum of 18.
- A caregiver collecting a Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription shows government photo ID even though the patient collecting the same fill would not need to.
- A Schedule II Controlled Prescription fill waits in will-call for 7 calendar days from its ready date; a Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription fill for 5.
